### Project Name

OpenEnv

### Project Description

OpenEnv is a unified framework for building, deploying, and interacting with isolated execution environments for agentic reinforcement learning (RL). It exposes simple, Gymnasium-style APIs (reset, step, state) and uses MCP as the interface between model and environment. Environments are packaged as containers, published to the Hugging Face Hub, and consumed by any trainer, harness, or evaluator that speaks the spec.

The project solves a fragmentation problem. Trainers expect environments in their own format, eval suites ship their own runners, and each agentic harness runs differently. An environment, harness, or trajectory built for one stack rarely works with another. OpenEnv provides a thin, neutral set of contracts so that work written once runs on any stack.

OpenEnv launched in October 2025 as a joint project between Hugging Face and Meta (Meta-PyTorch), introduced at the PyTorch Conference. In June 2026 the repository moved to huggingface/OpenEnv and stewardship broadened to a multi-company Technical Committee. Today it has 2,300+ GitHub stars, 4,200+ environments on the Hugging Face Hub, a 21,000+ member Discord, and hosted hackathons with 40,000+ submissions. 

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

OpenEnv fits AAIF's goal of giving agentic AI neutral, open infrastructure. AAIF hosts the standards agents use when they run in production, such as MCP and AGENTS.md. OpenEnv covers the stage before that: training and evaluating agents with reinforcement learning. Its model-to-environment interface is MCP, so an environment built for RL exposes the same tool interface the agent calls once it is deployed. That keeps how agents are trained consistent with how they run.

OpenEnv is already multi-vendor, with a Technical Committee spanning ten companies. Under AAIF, contributors get vendor-neutral governance for a shared environment spec, and that spec can develop alongside MCP within the same foundation.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

- MCP: OpenEnv uses MCP as its model-to-environment interface. Environments expose tools over MCP, built on fastmcp. OpenEnv adds what RL training needs on top: episode lifecycle (reset, step), rewards and rubrics, isolation, and packaging.
- goose: goose is one of the agentic harnesses OpenEnv targets. [RFC 005](https://github.com/huggingface/OpenEnv/blob/main/rfcs/005-agentic-harnesses.md) defines a wrapping pattern so a harness can be trained and evaluated in OpenEnv environments while keeping its own control loop.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

**Use cases**
- RL post-training of LLMs on coding REPLs, browser control, tool use, and games (Wordle, Sudoku, OpenSpiel).
- Evaluating tool-using agents on realistic tasks ([Turing case study](https://huggingface.co/blog/openenv-turing)).
- Publishing environments once to the Hugging Face Hub and running them across trainers and sandbox providers, like [FineEnvs](https://huggingface.co/FineEnvs)
- Enterprise RL with OpenEnv and Foundry, [blogpost](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/outcome-driven-learning-systems-enterprise-rl-with-openenv-and-foundry/)

**Evidence of adoption**
- 4,200+ environments published to the [Hugging Face OpenEnv Hub](https://huggingface.co/openenv); 2,300+ GitHub stars; 21,000+ Discord members.
- Technical Committee members: Meta-PyTorch, Reflection, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Prime Intellect, Mercor, Fleet AI, Modal, Unsloth, and Hugging Face.
- Integrated or supported by trainers and inference engines including TRL, Unsloth, SkyRL (UC Berkeley), Axolotl, Lightning AI, vLLM, and SGLang.
- Sandbox backends shipped as optional integrations: Modal, Daytona, Azure Container Apps, Novita.
- Data and environment partners: Scale AI, Surge AI, Snorkel AI, Patronus AI, Turing, Halluminate, Scorecard, Scaler AI Labs.
- Events: a 200-person hackathon in San Francisco (March 2026), a ~2,000-attendee hackathon in India with Scaler AI Labs (April 2026), the AgentBeats workshop with UC Berkeley, and a GPU MODE lecturel

### Governance Model

OpenEnv runs a lightweight governance model built on shared ownership. A multi-company Technical Committee (Meta-PyTorch, Reflection, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Prime Intellect, Mercor, Fleet AI, Modal, Unsloth, Hugging Face) meets biweekly on roadmap, technical direction, RFCs, work allocation, partnerships, and community events. Work happens asynchronously on GitHub (issues, PRs, RFCs) and Slack, and the meeting exists to unblock it. Technical authority is earned by individuals through PRs, commits, and reviews. 

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

GitHub Actions runs tests (pytest), lint (ruff), and environment lockfile validation on every PR and push to main. Further workflows build Docker images for environments, deploy environments to Hugging Face Spaces, validate the environment runtime, and build docs per PR. Releases are cut from v*.*.* tags and published to PyPI (TestPyPI first). Cadence is weekly: v0.4.2 (Sep 9), v0.5.0 (Sep 17), v0.6.0 (Sep 24, 2026).

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

Spec changes go through the public RFC process in [rfcs/README.md](https://github.com/huggingface/OpenEnv/blob/main/rfcs/README.md). New core APIs, breaking changes, architectural decisions, and new abstractions need an RFC, filed as a PR (or via the RFC issue template). RFCs move through review. Eight RFCs to date: 001 to 004 shipped (abstractions, environment spec, MCP support, rubrics); 005 to 008 in PR or review (agentic harnesses, multi-component rewards, environment datasets, auto-validation). General contributions follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/huggingface/OpenEnv/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

The Technical Committee has one representative per member organization, with Ben Burtenshaw (Hugging Face) as technical lead and Emre Guven (Reflection) as GTM lead. Decisions are made by consensus on GitHub and at the biweekly sync. Significant technical changes require an accepted RFC. Contributors move up a ladder from reviewing RFCs to owning one end to end, which is how partner organizations take ownership of components.

### Roadmap

The next 12 months move OpenEnv from environments that are easy to publish toward environments that are validated and trainable, and toward a library that connects harness, environment, and trainer for any model:

RFC | Topic | Theme | Status
-- | -- | -- | --
005 | Agentic harness integration  | Harnesses | In review
006 | Harness interception: token capture contract for black-box harnesses (capture proxy merged in #1036) | Harnesses | In review
008 | Environment auto-validation (openenv validate) and trainability bar (#778) | Rewards and validation | In review
009 | openenvd: privileged sidecar with policy-scoped surfaces (agent, grader, telemetry) | Rewards and validation | Draft
011 | GRPO harness training recipes per framework | Training | Draft
012 | Harbor capture purpose, provider fidelity, live-session ownership | Harnesses | In review
013 | Task sampling, curriculum, and in-training evaluation | Training | In review


### Security

No OpenSSF Best Practices badge yet. 

Current posture: GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs with least-privilege permissions, Dependabot updates, automated security analysis on PRs, and per-environment lockfile validation in CI. Environments run isolated in containers or remote sandboxes. Vulnerabilities are reported privately.
